title: Untitled: THEY say of poets, they must…
text: THEY say of poets, they must be born such: so must mathematicians, so must great generals, and so indeed must all other denominations of men, or it is not possible they should excel. But with whatever faculties we are born, and to whatever studies our genius may direct us, studies they must still be. I am persuaded that Milton did not write his Paradise Lost, nor Homer his Iliad, nor Newton his Principia, without immense labour. Nature gave them a bias towards their respective pursuits, and that strong propensity, I suppose, we mean by genius. The rest they gave themselves.
